propositions: merge.ours.driver is set per clone in init.py but never committed, so the reconcile-bridge.yml workflow does not inherit it on the runner
The .bridge_state/* merge=ours gitattribute names an undefined driver on the runner, causing git to fall back to a 3-way text merge of the 18M-byte JSON file instead of local-wins behavior
reconcile-bridge.yml performs a bare git worktree add without calling rebar init, unlike reconcile-bridge-canary.yml which calls rebar init and thus already obtains the driver
blob:none filtering during reconverge will lazily materialize large blobs mid-merge if the driver is undefined, causing fragile path failures
The fix requires setting merge.ours.driver=true in reconcile-bridge.yml before any merge step, with unit and integration test coverage for both the fixed and broken scenarios
